Bank Deposits ↔ Checking Accounts the single strongest relationship in the dataset
0.84
Bank Deposits ↔ Saving Accounts customers who deposit heavily also carry it into savings

Business Lending ↔ Bank Loans some customers carry both personal and business debt

The high correlation between Bank Deposits and Saving Accounts suggests they largely measure overlapping financial behavior — customers who actively deposit funds also tend to maintain or grow their savings balance. — insight recorded directly in Project_2.ipynb
0 missing values across all 25 columns, and zero duplicate client records — the dataset needed no repair before analysis
HOLDS UP ACROSS THE DATA
  • Jade-tier customers carry the largest share of deposits, loans and business lending alike
  • Adult and senior-citizen customers hold far higher average deposits than young customers
  • Age shows almost no linear relationship with any single account balance
  • Properties Owned correlates weakly with every banking variable (−0.03 to 0.02)
  • 64% of customers hold just one credit card; only 10% hold three

03 — CUSTOMER SEGMENTS

Every customer sits in one of four loyalty tiers

Jade, Silver, Gold and Platinum — the bank's own segmentation, profiled against deposits, loans and average balance.

1,331
44.37% of customers · $927M deposits (46%)
Jade
The largest tier by headcount and by dollar volume — $806M in loans (45%) and $927M in deposits, more than any other tier combined against Silver.
767
25.57% of customers · $505M deposits
Silver
Second-largest segment — $453M in loans, a solid mid-volume base that tracks Jade's shape at roughly half the scale.
585
19.50% of customers · $389M deposits
Gold
$336M in loans and the smallest gap between deposits and lending of any tier — a proportionally even book.
317
10.57% of customers · $194M deposits
Platinum
Smallest tier by headcount, but average balance per customer ($612K) sits within 12% of every other tier — loyalty status tracks engagement here, not net worth.
FROM THE NOTEBOOK'S FINAL CELLS — Project_2.ipynb
  • Bank Deposits and Saving Accounts move together — likely the same underlying financial behavior
  • Age and Estimated Income show moderate ties to Superannuation, Savings and Checking balances — a lifecycle effect
  • Properties Owned depends on factors outside this dataset — its correlations stay weak across the board
  • Business Lending tracks Bank Loans but stays largely independent of deposit and property variables
